title: Password Security & Management Policy Template
metaDescription: Free password security policy template for businesses. Covers strong passwords, 2FA, password managers, and security best practices.
description: A comprehensive password security and management policy template designed for businesses and organizations. This template helps establish clear guidelines for password creation, management, and security practices to protect against data breaches and unauthorized access.

sections.heading: Policy Overview and Purpose
sections.content: This Password Security and Management Policy establishes guidelines for creating, managing, and protecting passwords across {{organization_name}}. This policy aims to safeguard sensitive information, prevent unauthorized access, and reduce security risks associated with weak password practices. All employees, contractors, and authorized users must comply with these requirements to maintain our organization's cybersecurity standards.

sections.heading: Password Creation Requirements
sections.content: All passwords must meet the following minimum requirements: minimum {{min_length}} characters in length, contain a combination of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters. Passwords must not contain dictionary words, personal information (names, birthdays, addresses), or common patterns (123456, password, qwerty). Passwords should be unique and not reused across multiple accounts or systems within {{password_reuse_period}}.

sections.heading: Password Manager Requirements
sections.content: All users must utilize an approved password manager to generate, store, and manage passwords. Approved password managers include {{approved_managers}}. The organization will provide licenses or reimburse costs for approved password management solutions. Users must enable the password manager's security features including master password protection and encryption. Personal password managers may be used for work accounts only if they meet our security standards and approval process.

sections.heading: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Requirements
sections.content: Multi-factor authentication must be enabled on all accounts that support it, including but not limited to email, cloud services, administrative systems, and financial platforms. Acceptable MFA methods include authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy), hardware security keys, SMS verification (as a last resort), and biometric authentication where available. Users must register backup MFA methods and store recovery codes securely. MFA must not be disabled without explicit approval from {{security_contact}}.

sections.heading: Password Storage and Sharing Policies
sections.content: Passwords must never be written down in plain text, stored in unsecured documents, shared via email or messaging, or disclosed to unauthorized individuals. When password sharing is necessary for shared accounts, it must be done through approved password managers with appropriate access controls. Temporary passwords must be changed immediately upon first use. Default passwords on any systems or devices must be changed before deployment. Use secure browsing practices, including private browsers like a privacy-focused browser when accessing sensitive accounts on shared devices.

sections.heading: Password Change and Maintenance
sections.content: Passwords must be changed immediately if compromise is suspected, upon employee termination or role changes, after security incidents involving the account, and when prompted by security systems. Regular password changes are required every {{change_frequency}} for high-privilege accounts. Users must monitor their accounts for suspicious activity and report any security concerns immediately to {{reporting_contact}}. Participate in security awareness training and stay informed about current password security best practices.

placeholders.label: Password Change Frequency for High-Privilege Accounts

sections.heading: Incident Response and Violations
sections.content: Users must immediately report suspected password compromises, unauthorized access attempts, phishing attempts, or security breaches to {{incident_contact}}. Upon notification of a potential breach, users must immediately change affected passwords and review account activity. Violations of this password policy may result in {{violation_consequences}}. The organization will provide support and training to help users comply with these requirements. Regular security assessments will be conducted to ensure policy effectiveness and compliance.

placeholders.label: Consequences for Policy Violations
placeholders.defaultValue: disciplinary action, additional security training, or account restrictions

Companies responding to security incidents or breaches
